scope: Diagnostic source/historical-render inspection; no new render acceptance or geographic identity certification
conclusion: The first cheap-model bottleneck is colour/uncertainty and reference quality. Several game comparisons additionally lack source-visible facade detail. Fine-tuning broad material classes before correcting those stages is not justified.

gateCases.finding: Saved game view is mostly a blank brick wall while source shows repeated openings, arches and contrasting heads. Verify the rendered face and detail delivery before treating this as a texture-training example.
Severe upper exposure loss; visible right/bottom masonry supports brick but exact target boundary is not certified. Local model already identifies brick in full image; tighter crop gives no benefit.
Source shows varied warm masonry and pale trim; saved focused game view is a plain uniform ochre wall. Colour label buff versus model brown is not an albedo measurement.
Native source visibly has brick courses and arched masonry heads. Corrected the pilot material reference from unknown to brick. Saved game appears darker; no exact colour or texture scale acceptance.
Broad dark blue-grey appearance is visible; substrate/finish is unresolved. Both local inputs answer render/grey. Keep the substrate unknown rather than promoting model confidence.
Source is ochre/buff; model says brown under both input crops. Saved game is paler and smoother. Historical cream-variant evidence supports a separate warmer palette member; no exact colour match.
Source is a narrow articulated brick frontage; saved focused game view is mostly an unarticulated strip. Resolve wall/view identity and detail residency before buying appearance inference.

Contextual game view is substantially tree-occluded. Earlier isolated pale-cream trial improved direction only. Tighter source crop changes local cream answer to grey, reducing reference compatibility.
Source reads white/pale smooth facade with dark trim and distinctive openings. Saved game changes silhouette/opening layout and appears beige. Broad material extraction already returns render/white.
Brown brick is recognised in both inputs. Saved game retains coarse window rhythm but loses decorative pale horizontal/arched features. Material-family classification cannot supply those assemblies.

postHocDisagreementReview.scope: Inspected after seeing model outputs; cannot be treated as independent held-out ground truth
postHocDisagreementReview.finding: Several unresolved references visibly contain masonry, mixed assemblies or ambiguous finish, rather than uniformly unusable evidence. Do not turn all thirteen disagreements into negative training labels. Re-audit unknown substrate, mixed material, poor visibility and uncertain identity separately.

tasks: Adjudicate unresolved and minority material examples with explicit visible support, independent of model answers.
Use a palette-selection task with illumination uncertainty rather than predicting precise photo RGB or forcing every warm hue into one bin.
For source/render cases 0, 3 and 15, verify facade orientation and feature delivery before texture changes.
Keep exact texture scale and material masks unaccepted until measured; do not export current pilot as image-edit training pairs.
